description: Python ecosystem groupings (pep621/uv/poetry). Peer-dep coupled stacks bundled together.

packageRules.description: Don't track `python` via the native pep621 manager — `requires-python` is normally a min-version metadata range (`>=3.10`), not a runtime pin, so the pep621 view of it must not bump. Exact `==X.Y.Z` pins ARE tracked, but via the custom manager below + the `python-version` datasource, which surfaces a separate `python` dep that this rule does not touch.

Group the exact-pinned `requires-python` (custom manager below, depName `python`) into the same PR as the `python` Docker base image (dockerfile manager, also depName `python`) so an exact CPython pin and its base image never bump separately and drift apart. Split, NEITHER half can go green: the base-image-only PR fails `No interpreter found for Python <old>` (pyproject still pins the old triple, and UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never forces the mismatch to fail loudly) and the pyproject-only PR fails `The current Python version is not compatible with the locked Python requirement` — owine/trip-tracker #180/#182. Both spellings are listed because `FROM docker.io/library/python:X` yields the fully-qualified depName rather than the bare `python`, mirroring docker.json's runtime-major label rule; plain strings are glob-matched with `.`/`/` literal, so these match exactly and leave `python-slim`/`my.registry/python` alone. This holds regardless of `extends` order ONLY because docker.json's `dockerfile bases` rule negates these same two names — that rule matches `matchManagers: [dockerfile]`, so with :python extended before :docker it would otherwise win the groupName and pull the base image back out. Keep this list and that negation in sync. MAJORS: intentionally no `matchUpdateTypes` — the group applies to majors too, because a runtime major has exactly the same drift hazard as a patch and the two deps always bump to the same version. This does not weaken the fleet's major policy: default.json's `separateMajorMinor`/`separateMultipleMajor` still isolate the major onto its own branch, and its major rule still applies the 7-day soak, `automerge: false`, `feat:` type, and `major-update`/`needs-review` labels. Grouping only decides which deps share that branch, not how it is reviewed.

customManagers.description: Track an EXACT-pinned `requires-python = "==X.Y.Z"` in pyproject.toml against the CPython runtime (datasource `python-version`, depName `python`) so it bumps in lockstep with the `python` Docker base image. Tolerant of formatting: single OR double TOML quotes and optional whitespace around `=`/`==` all match; a trailing inline comment after the closing quote is unaffected since the match ends at the quote. Anchored to the `==`-triple form only: floor ranges (`>=3.10`), compatible ranges (`~=3.14`), and wildcard pins (`==3.14.*`) do NOT match, so non-exact-pin consumers are a no-op. The `==` is literal context outside the capture; only the `X.Y.Z` triple is replaced. CONFLICT RESOLUTION: if the system Python ever fails to satisfy this exact pin, uv silently falls back to a uv-managed standalone interpreter (unreachable by a non-root runtime user) — consumers MUST set `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never` so that mismatch fails the build loudly instead. MANUAL STEP REQUIRED — a `python runtime` PR lands RED and needs one hand-authored `uv lock` commit pushed to its branch before CI can pass. uv.lock carries its OWN `requires-python`, and nothing in this preset can refresh it: a custom regex manager performs a text substitution and runs no lockfile update, and `postUpgradeTasks` (which could shell out to `uv lock`) is unavailable on the Mend-hosted app this fleet uses. Until that commit is pushed, every uv job fails `The current Python version (<new>) is not compatible with the locked Python requirement: ==<old>`. Lockfile maintenance does eventually reconcile uv.lock, but on its own mon/wed/fri/sun schedule and on a DIFFERENT branch — it will not unblock the open PR.
